reason: Answering my guests myself, even at midnight, is my hospitality and why they come back and leave good reviews. It is not expensive, but I don't want a machine talking to my guests in my name, and the Wi-Fi password is already on a card on the fridge.
objection: Guests will feel they are talking to a robot instead of the host, and if it tells a German family something wrong about parking or check-in, it is my review that suffers, not the company's. And I still worry what happens with my guests' data, paper agreement or not.
would_change_my_mind: If another host I know on the coast used it for a whole season and showed me it cut the night messages without guests complaining, and my son checked the GDPR agreement and said it is fine.
